newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Summers sees bigger IMF monitoring role.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Summers sees bigger IMF monitoring role.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund should play a greater role in monitoring the health of national financial systems in emerging market countries, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Tuesday.
In a speech prepared for delivery to the Fifth Annual Conference on the Americas, he said the IMF must recognize that it needs to expand its role beyond a merely fiscal one.
"It needs to recognize the threat that financial system vulnerabilities pose to macroeconomic stability and to take a more active role in addressing them," Summers said.
A text of his remarks was issued in Washington.

Summers noted that the Group of Seven industrial countries -- the United States, Japan, Canada, Britain, France, Germany and Italy -- were working toward an accord on how to bolster financial systems to foster development in emerging markets.

He said one way to do so was by having strong banking supervision that included tough entry requirements, prudent rules for capital, liquidity and currency exposure and a framework for dealing with insolvent institutions.
As well, supervisors need a framework for dealing with problem banks and systemic risks, as well as strong accounting standards up to international standards, Summers said.
Policy changes were needed at the international level, including enhanced surveillance by the IMF, as well as financial sector lending by multilateral development banks when needed.

Summers said that U.S. success in cutting its deficit was "perhaps the single most important factor for promoting financial stability and economic development in Latin America" because it meant a calmer global interest rate environment.

The economic outlook was good for developing countries in Latin America and, in future, he hoped reforms now under way would reduce the economic volatility that some countries have experienced in the past.
